Alibaba Group and AliExpress: A Global E-commerce Powerhouse
Alibaba Group, founded by Jack Ma in 1999, has evolved from a small B2B marketplace into one of the world’s largest technology and retail conglomerates. Its mission—to make it easy to do business anywhere—is realized through a massive ecosystem that connects manufacturers, wholesalers, and individual consumers globally.

At the heart of the group is Alibaba.com, the world’s leading platform for B2B (Business-to-Business) trade. It serves as a bridge for entrepreneurs and companies to source products in bulk directly from Chinese factories. This is the go-to destination for business owners looking to develop private labels or secure wholesale inventory at competitive prices.

In contrast, AliExpress operates on a B2C (Business-to-Consumer) model. It allows individual shoppers from around the world to buy single items at near-wholesale rates. While Alibaba.com is built for logistics and bulk shipping, AliExpress is designed for retail convenience, making it a favorite for global consumers and dropshippers alike.

Beyond just shopping, Alibaba Group’s strength lies in its integrated infrastructure, including Cainiao for logistics and Alipay for secure digital payments. As of 2026, the company continues to lead by integrating advanced AI and Cloud computing to streamline the global supply chain, maintaining its status as a titan of modern commerce
